source: a 3d racing game where you race against the computer. dont ask for input just build the game

questions.ask: What visual setting should the race track use (for example, modern city streets, a desert circuit, forest roads, or a futuristic neon course)?
Should the race take place on a closed loop circuit or a point-to-point track with a finish line?

answers.ask: What visual setting should the race track use (for example, modern city streets, a desert circuit, forest roads, or a futuristic neon course)?
answers.answer: Use a simple modern city street setting, with clean roads, barriers, and a straightforward arcade racing look.

answers.ask: Should the race take place on a closed loop circuit or a point-to-point track with a finish line?
answers.answer: Use a small closed-loop circuit so the player and computer opponent can race multiple laps.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D racing map set on a small closed-loop circuit through simple modern city streets. Clean paved roads form the loop, bordered by racing barriers, with a straightforward arcade racing composition.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Racing: a lap-based race against one computer opponent.

### Shape and preset
Use `route-circuit`, a compact, closed, drivable loop through modern city streets. Match the Circuit Racing preset; its circuit form, starting grid, lap sensing, and physical barriers remain appropriate.

### Config requirements
Use `barrier-guardrail` as clean continuous racing barriers along both road edges and around corners. Use `startpoint-line` as a visible start/finish stripe on one straight, `spawn-grid` as two side-by-side launch slots, and `trigger-finish` as the visible finish-line gate/stripe at that same location.

### Layout requirements
Place `startpoint-line` and one two-slot `spawn-grid` on the widest straight, with the player and computer opponent aligned side by side facing the first corner. Place one `trigger-finish` across that same start/finish line. Place `trigger-lap` at the start/finish line, spanning the full road width so each completed loop is registered. No recovery checkpoints are required for this short, barrier-contained circuit.

### Layout components
Build one small city-block circuit: a clean paved asphalt road forming a legible closed loop with broad turns and a clear start/finish straight. Low racing barriers continuously define the drivable course and prevent shortcutting through the city blocks. Surround the loop with simple modern urban frontage, sidewalks, sparse street furniture, and restrained building facades as non-enterable scenery. Keep the boundary visually enclosed by the street barriers and city-edge facades. Compose the circuit as a readable compact loop in plan view, with the start straight prominent in the foreground.

### Render order
Use `authored_plan`: the closed circuit must be valid by construction, continuously connected, and unambiguously followable before the city dressing is applied.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small, driven by a compact multi-lap circuit for two racers. Theme is clean modern city streets with a straightforward arcade-racing register. Use `P6` because the circuit route must be generated as a valid closed track.

iso_prompt:
Create a 3D racing map set on a small closed-loop circuit through simple modern city streets. Clean paved roads form the loop, bordered by racing barriers, with a straightforward arcade racing composition.

LAYOUT FEATURES for this Racing map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Lap Circuit: A closed loop run a set number of times.

INCLUDE:
- Physical Guardrail: Walls and rails that actually block the racer, as opposed to painted lane markings that only indicate.
- Start Line: The marked start position - a painted line or a lane slot on the track.
- Multi-Lane Starting Grid: A wide launch front of evenly spaced slots - blocks in a pool, lanes on a track, grid spots on a circuit - laid out side by side.
- Terminal Finish: The built finish at the exact end of the course - a touch-pad wall, a finish line across the track, or a finish gate.

The reference image is a true overhead top-down view of this scene and it is the GROUND TRUTH for the layout. Rebuild the SAME scene as a polished isometric three-quarter aerial view. Keep the racing loop EXACTLY as it is - the same closed circuit, the same corners in the same places, the same straights, the same road width and the same start and finish positions. Do NOT add, remove, move, narrow or close any part of the track. The loop stays the only road in the image: no extra road, spur, shortcut or second track. Keep the SAME materials, surface colours, textures, props and lighting as the reference. CAMERA: this is the one thing that changes. The reference looks straight down; tilt to a true three-quarter aerial view of about 45 degrees and rotate it, so the scene reads as a 3D diorama rather than a flat plan. Side faces MUST now be visible - tree trunks under their canopies, the walls of buildings, the face of any tunnel mouth, the thickness of the ground - and the far side of the scene sits higher in the frame than the near side. Keep the angle steep enough that the whole loop stays visible end to end rather than hidden behind scenery. No characters, labels, UI, borders or watermark.
td_prompt:
Build a clean straight-overhead TOP-DOWN (nadir) low-poly Roblox 3D scene, richly themed from this description:
Create a 3D racing map set on a small closed-loop circuit through simple modern city streets. Clean paved roads form the loop, bordered by racing barriers, with a straightforward arcade racing composition.

LAYOUT FEATURES for this Racing map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Lap Circuit: A closed loop run a set number of times.

INCLUDE:
- Physical Guardrail: Walls and rails that actually block the racer, as opposed to painted lane markings that only indicate.
- Start Line: The marked start position - a painted line or a lane slot on the track.
- Multi-Lane Starting Grid: A wide launch front of evenly spaced slots - blocks in a pool, lanes on a track, grid spots on a circuit - laid out side by side.
- Terminal Finish: The built finish at the exact end of the course - a touch-pad wall, a finish line across the track, or a finish gate.
The reference image is the AUTHORED TRACK PLAN for this scene, seen from directly overhead, and it is the GROUND TRUTH for the layout. The light band is the drivable road surface and it forms ONE continuous closed loop; the dark field around it is everything that is not road; the GREEN line across the band marks WHERE the start/finish sits - build a real start/finish there in this scene's own style, a painted or checkered line across the full road width, rather than copying a coloured stripe. Reproduce that route EXACTLY - the same loop, the same corners in the same places and the same directions, the same straights, the same road width throughout, and the markings where they are. The loop must stay continuous with no break, no dead end and no fork. That loop is the ONLY drivable surface anywhere in the image, and it has no stub, spur or dead end of surface attached to it, however short. Everything the description asks for is realised ON it: a boost pad, arrow chevron, speed strip, jump ramp, chicane or obstacle is painted or built flush INTO the loop's own surface where the loop runs, never as a separate slab, apron, platform or approach laid on the ground beside it. A tunnel exists only where the loop itself passes through a hill and comes out the other side - do NOT build a tunnel mouth, cave entrance, gate or arch that the track does not run through. A bridge is a stretch of the loop crossing water. Do NOT lay any extra road, spur, shortcut, slip road, pit lane, service track, parallel carriageway or second track, and leave the ground on either side of the loop free of drivable surface entirely. Do NOT copy the grey and dark colours of the reference - it encodes the route only. Take the materials, surface colours, textures, lighting and mood entirely from the scene description above, and dress the surroundings with its named props and scenery. Barriers, kerbs, stands, trees, buildings and scenery sit BESIDE the road and never on it: the full width of the track stays clear and drivable end to end. CAMERA: straight down at 90 degrees, a true nadir view, with ZERO perspective and ZERO isometric tilt. Show ONLY the tops of things - the road surface, tree canopies, roofs - and NO side faces of any kind: no building walls, no tree trunks, no cliff or rock faces, no visible tunnel arch, no vertical surface anywhere. Objects at the edges of the image are seen from directly above exactly as those in the middle are, with no lean or splay. No labels, UI, borders or watermark.
